title: Roots and Patterns
description: Hebrew words can be organized by consonantal roots and recurring word patterns. This unit introduces the analytical method and its limits.

blocks.html: Many Hebrew roots contain three consonants. A pattern places vowels and sometimes additional consonants around the root to form a noun, adjective, or verb. Several words may share a root but differ in grammatical form and meaning. Root analysis helps organize vocabulary; it does not reliably predict an unfamiliar word's meaning, so confirm each form in a lexicon.

didYouKnow: According to OSHB/MorphHB (CC BY 4.0), the most frequent word in this unit is מַמְלָכָה (mamlāḵāh), occurring 43 times in the Westminster Leningrad Codex.
